chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man came out of a ship naked, or his clothes were stripped from him, and he found nothing to pray in.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray by gestures. If it was a woman, she places her hand over her private part, and if it was a man, he places his hand over his private part. Then they sit and gesture with their heads, neither prostrating nor bowing, lest what is behind them be exposed. Their prayer is gesturing with their heads.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if they were in water or a deep sea, they do not prostrate upon it, and the direction (facing the Qiblah) is lifted from them. They gesture in that with gestures; their raising (of heads) is considered facing the Qiblah, and their lowering (is considered prostration).'

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: Gesturing (with head/eyes) as a substitute for physical movements in prayer

ai.seo_question: How does one perform prayer when naked or without clothes according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the fiqh of 'Salat al-Musafir' or prayer in extreme necessity, where the Imam (peace be upon him) instructs that a naked person prays by nodding with the head, keeping hands over the private parts to minimize exposure, and omitting full Ruku' and Sajdah. The ruling extends to those in the sea, where the direction of prayer is determined by the orientation of the head movements, reflecting the principle of 'Yusr' (ease) in Islamic jurisprudence when full ritual requirements are impossible to fulfill.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far, ‘A man comes out from a ship naked, or his clothes have been looted and he cannot find anything he can pray Salāt in’. So heasws said: ‘He should pray Salāt by gestures. So if it was a woman, she would make her hand to be upon her private part, and if it was a man he should place his hand upon his private part. Then they would sit indicating with gestures, neither perform Sajdah nor perform Rukū lest what is behind them be exposed. Their Salāt would be gesturing by their heads’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And if they were both in water, or sea waves, they would not perform Sajdah upon it, and the direction (facing Qiblah) would be dropped from them in it. They would be indicating in that with gestures, the direction (Qiblah) having been Raised from them and their ablutions’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who sails in a boat while naked or his clothes are looted and does not find anything to perform Salah (prayer) with. He (the Imam) said, ‘He performs Salah (prayer) by making gestures and a woman in such condition places her hand over her vagina, and if a man, he places his hand over his private part. They sit and make gestures and do not perform Sajdah (prostration) or Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees) so their back is exposed. Their Salah (prayer) is by gestures by their heads.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘If they are in water or sea with waves they do not perform Sajdah (prostration) and they are exempt from facing (the direction of al- Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah)). They make gestures: their rising and lowering is gestures.’”
